title: Previous Approval Requirement for Central Authority Regulations

content.scenario: The Central Authority issues a regulation without obtaining the previous approval of the Central Government, citing urgency and public interest.
content.outcome: The regulation is invalid, as the Central Authority failed to obtain the previous approval of the Central Government, which is a mandatory requirement under Section 104(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The Central Authority must follow the prescribed procedure for making regulations, including obtaining previous approval, to ensure validity.

user_queries: Is previous approval of the Central Government required for Central Authority regulations?
What are the consequences of issuing regulations without previous approval?
Can the Central Authority issue regulations without following the prescribed procedure?
